v1AgentSessionStatus.description:
AgentSessionStatus represents the abstract state of the AI agent running in a session.
Provider-agnostic: works for any AI agent (Claude, etc.), not tied to a specific provider.

 - AGENT_SESSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: No agent activity or agent not configured.
 - AGENT_SESSION_STATUS_WORKING: Agent is actively processing.
 - AGENT_SESSION_STATUS_WAITING_FOR_INPUT: Agent is waiting for user input (permission prompt, elicitation, etc.).
 - AGENT_SESSION_STATUS_IDLE: Agent finished processing and is idle (waiting at the prompt).

v1AndroidEmulatorConfig.description:
AndroidEmulatorConfig is a session's resolved Android emulator configuration
(SessionTemplateSnapshot.android_emulator), produced from the
CreateSessionRequest.device_spec / preview link device spec that booted it.
Empty fields fall back to platform defaults.

coldBoot.description:
Boot the emulator cold (-no-snapshot-load) and never save a quickboot
snapshot, so every boot is a full first boot.

cores.description:
Emulator CPU core count. 0 = sized to the host (cores/2, clamped to
[2, 4]). The VM clamps out-of-range values, always leaving the host a core.

deviceProfile.description: avdmanager device profile (for example, "pixel_7"). Empty = platform default.

ramMb.description:
Emulator RAM in MB. 0 = sized to the host (RAM/4, clamped to [2048, 6144]).
The VM clamps out-of-range values to what the host can spare.

systemImage.description:
sdkmanager system image package (for example,
"system-images;android-36;google_apis_ps16k;x86_64"). Empty = platform default.

v1AutoMappedInput.description:
AutoMappedInput records a template session input that was auto-filled from
the caller's saved inputs because map_saved_to_session_inputs was set.

savedInputId.description: ID of the saved input used to populate the value.

sessionInputKey.description: Key of the template session input that was auto-filled.

v1ClusterOption.description: ClusterOption represents a single cluster that can serve a given image + machine type.

v1CompareSessionTemplateResponse.description: CompareSessionTemplateResponse contains both the snapshot and current template configurations.

changedVariableKeys.description:
Keys of template variables whose values differ between snapshot and current.
Only the keys are returned; actual values are never exposed.

current.description: Current template configuration (null if the template is deleted).

snapshot.description: Template configuration from the session's snapshot (at creation time).

expiresAt.description:
When the link expires. Opens after this are refused; devices already
open are unaffected and end on their own auto-terminate window.

jti.description:
The link's id, also embedded in the token. Sessions this link spawns
record it, so it is the handle for finding and stopping them.

token.description:
The signed link token ("<base64url payload>.<base64url signature>").
Treat it as a bearer credential: it is the whole of what a viewer needs.
Most callers want url instead.

url.description:
The shareable viewer URL — post this on the pull request or paste it into
chat.

v1CreateSavedInputRequest.description: CreateSavedInputRequest is the request for creating a saved input.

isSecret.description: Whether this is a secret value.

v1CreateSavedInputResponse.description: CreateSavedInputResponse is the response for creating a saved input.

v1CreateSessionResponse.description: CreateSessionResponse is the response for creating a session.

autoMappedInputs.description:
Session inputs that were auto-filled from the user's saved inputs.
Empty unless the request set map_saved_to_session_inputs=true.

v1CreateTemplateResponse.description: CreateTemplateResponse is the response for creating a template.

v1DeleteSavedInputResponse.description: DeleteSavedInputResponse is the response for deleting a saved input.

v1DeleteSessionResponse.description: DeleteSessionResponse is the response for deleting a session.

v1DeleteTemplateResponse.description: DeleteTemplateResponse is the response for deleting a template.

v1DeleteTerminatedSessionsResponse.description: DeleteTerminatedSessionsResponse is the response for deleting all terminated sessions.

deletedCount.description: Number of sessions that were deleted.

v1FeatureFlag.description: FeatureFlag represents a toggleable feature for a template.

description.description: Description explaining what this feature flag enables.

v1FeatureFlagCreate.description: FeatureFlagCreate is used when creating a feature flag.

description.description: Description explaining what this feature flag enables.

v1GetMeResponse.description: GetMeResponse is the response containing the current authenticated user.

v1GetSavedInputResponse.description: GetSavedInputResponse is the response for getting a saved input.

v1GetSessionLogsResponse.description: GetSessionLogsResponse is a single log chunk in the stream.

heartbeatMessage.description: Whether this is a heartbeat message (empty content, just keeping connection alive).

v1GetSessionResponse.description: GetSessionResponse is the response for getting a session.

v1GetTemplateResponse.description: GetTemplateResponse is the response for getting a template.

v1GetWorkspaceInfoResponse.description:
GetWorkspaceInfoResponse carries workspace-level capabilities the UI uses to
tailor what it shows.

androidEmulatorAvailable.description:
Whether the Android emulator capability (and the service ports that expose
it) is enabled for this workspace (rollout feature flag). Gates the
emulator service ports on templates and Android device_spec on sessions.

canViewUsage.description:
Whether the caller may see the workspace usage page (org permission
"view_billing_data" — workspace owners and billing-managing custom
roles). Gates the Usage navigation item in the UI; GetWorkspaceUsage
enforces the same permission server-side.

devicePreviewAvailable.description:
Whether device preview links and streaming are enabled for this workspace
(rollout feature flag). Gates minting/resolving preview links and the
viewer affordances in the UI.

gitProviderIntegrationAvailable.description:
Whether the git provider integration feature is enabled for this workspace
(rollout feature flag). Gates the integration section in the UI.

iosSimulatorAvailable.description:
Whether the iOS simulator capability is enabled for this workspace
(rollout feature flag). Gates requesting an iOS device on sessions.

isFreeTrial.description:
Whether the workspace is on a free trial. Free-trial sessions are pinned to
an 8-hour auto-terminate window that cannot be changed.

v1GetWorkspaceUsageResponse.description:
GetWorkspaceUsageResponse is the workspace usage report: a point-in-time
snapshot of who is running how many active sessions, on how many vCPUs and
how much memory, split by OS.

unknownMachineTypeCount.description:
Number of active sessions whose machine type had no resolvable vCPU/RAM
spec — those sessions are counted in session counts but contribute 0 to
the vcpu/memory sums, so totals may undercount when this is non-zero.

users.description:
Per-user breakdown, plus at most one workspace-owned bucket row.
Sorted by email for determinism; clients re-sort freely.

v1GitProviderConnectionStatus.description:
GitProviderConnectionStatus mirrors the monolith-side status of the user's
connected git provider account.

 - GIT_PROVIDER_CONNECTION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: Unknown status.
 - GIT_PROVIDER_CONNECTION_STATUS_NOT_CONNECTED: The user has never connected an account for this provider.
 - GIT_PROVIDER_CONNECTION_STATUS_CONNECTED: The user has a usable connection.
 - GIT_PROVIDER_CONNECTION_STATUS_ERROR: A connection exists but is unusable (grant revoked or token refresh failed);
the user must reconnect on the Bitrise connected-accounts page.

v1GitProviderIntegration.description:
GitProviderIntegration describes the state of the user's git provider
integration: the Bitrise-side connection status plus the RDE-side opt-in.

accountName.description: Provider-side account name (for example, the GitHub login). Empty unless connected.

accountUrl.description: Provider-side account URL. Empty unless connected.

connectionStatus.description: Status of the user's connected account on the Bitrise connected-accounts page.

enabled.description: Whether the user opted in to automatic git credential injection into their sessions.

v1Image.description:
Image represents a machine image available for sessions.

Deprecated: use Stack. Images expose opaque merged-stack ids (for example, "osx-26-edge")
that bundle many Xcode versions and can be recomposed at any time. Stack exposes
the stable, specific stack id with friendly metadata.

clusterName.description: The cluster where this image is available.

isDefault.description:
Whether this is the deployment's default image. Clients preselect it when
the user has made no prior choice. At most one image name is marked.

v1ListImagesResponse.description: ListImagesResponse is the response for listing images.

v1ListMachineTypesResponse.description: ListMachineTypesResponse is the response for listing machine types.

v1ListSavedInputsResponse.description: ListSavedInputsResponse is the response for listing saved inputs.

v1ListSessionNotificationsResponse.description: ListSessionNotificationsResponse is the response for listing session notifications.

v1ListSessionsResponse.description: ListSessionsResponse is the response for listing sessions.

v1ListStacksResponse.description: ListStacksResponse is the response for listing stacks.

v1ListTemplatesResponse.description: ListTemplatesResponse is the response for listing templates.

v1MachineType.description: MachineType represents a machine type available for sessions.

clusterName.description: The cluster where this machine type is available.

cpu.description: Display CPU string, for example, "4 vCPU".

isDefault.description:
Whether this is the deployment's default machine type. Clients preselect it
when the user has made no prior choice. At most one machine type name is
marked.

ram.description: Display RAM string, for example, "6 GB".

title.description:
Human-friendly title, for example, "M2 Pro Large". Empty when no friendly metadata
is available.

v1OpenRemoteAccessResponse.description: OpenRemoteAccessResponse is the response for opening remote access.

session.description: The updated session with remote access details.

v1PersistentDiskStatus.description:
PersistentDiskStatus represents the status of a machine's persistent disk.

 - PERSISTENT_DISK_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified or not applicable (non-terminated sessions).
 - PERSISTENT_DISK_STATUS_AVAILABLE: The disk is available and the session can be restored.
 - PERSISTENT_DISK_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE_SOON: The disk will become unavailable soon (within 1 week).
The session can still be restored but user should be warned.
 - PERSISTENT_DISK_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE: The disk is no longer available. The session cannot be restored.

v1PlatformUsage.description: PlatformUsage aggregates active sessions on one OS platform.

memoryGb.description: Total memory in GB across those sessions; unknown specs contribute 0.

sessionCount.description:
Number of active sessions (VM still consuming resources: starting,
running, terminating, or draining).

vcpu.description:
Total vCPUs across those sessions. Sessions whose machine type carries
no parseable spec contribute 0 (see unknown_machine_type_count).

v1PreviewArtifact.description:
PreviewArtifact identifies the app build a device session installs (a
preview link's session, or an ordinary session created with
CreateSessionRequest.artifact).

appName.description: App display name, echoed to the viewer page.

buildNumber.description: CI build number, echoed to the viewer page.

commitSha.description: Built commit SHA, echoed to the viewer page.

url.description:
Signed, expiring download URL for the app artifact. The session VM
downloads it directly — the backend never touches the bytes. It expires
independently of the link.

v1PreviewDeviceSpec.description:
PreviewDeviceSpec describes a virtual device: the one a preview link
requests (every open of the link spawns its own dedicated device session)
or the one an ordinary session boots (CreateSessionRequest.device_spec).
One vocabulary for both, so agents and CI describe devices the same way.

coldBoot.description:
Android only: boot the emulator cold (-no-snapshot-load) and never save a
quickboot snapshot, so every open exercises a full first boot.

cores.description:
Android only: emulator CPU core count. 0 = sized to the host (cores/2,
clamped). Same mint bound + on-VM clamp as ram_mb.

deviceModel.description: Device profile hint (for example, "pixel_7"). Empty = platform default.

osVersion.description:
iOS only: the simulator runtime to boot, as an iOS version such as "18.2"
(or a simctl runtime id). Anything else, and any value on Android, is
rejected. Empty = the newest installed runtime. Reads back as the version.

platform.description:
Device platform: "android" (emulator, Linux stacks) or "ios" (simulator,
macOS stacks).

ramMb.description:
Android only: emulator RAM in MB. 0 = sized to the host (RAM/4, clamped).
Bounded at mint against the machine type's specs; clamped again on the VM
with a degradation notice if the host cannot honor it.

systemImage.description:
Android only: sdkmanager system image package (for example,
"system-images;android-34;google_apis;x86_64"). Empty = platform
default. Images not pre-installed on the stack fall back to the best
installed one with a viewer-visible degradation notice — they are never
downloaded at boot.

v1PreviewDeviceState.description:
PreviewDeviceState is the device-readiness verdict carried on preview
resolves and on Session.device. A "running" session only means the startup script began — the
device (emulator/simulator) boots in the background for minutes more.
READY is asserted by the VM itself (via MachineReportDeviceReady) once the
device is booted AND the streamer delivers frames: the one authoritative
readiness fact consumers read instead of guessing from session status.

 - PREVIEW_DEVICE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED: No readiness verdict available (session predates the signal, or the
machine is not running yet). Consumers behave exactly as they did
before the signal existed.
 - PREVIEW_DEVICE_STATE_BOOTING: The machine is running but the VM has not yet proven its device usable.
 - PREVIEW_DEVICE_STATE_READY: The VM reported: device booted and streamer delivering frames.
 - PREVIEW_DEVICE_STATE_FAILED: The VM reported a terminal device failure for this boot (emulator never
booted, streamer never delivered a frame). Only ever asserted by the VM —
absence of a report stays UNSPECIFIED/BOOTING and consumers keep their
pre-signal bounded waits, so old VMs can never surface as FAILED.

v1PreviewInstallStatus.description:
PreviewInstallStatus is the state of the app install on a device — a
preview link's session (fired at claim) or a session created with an
artifact (fired at session start, re-fired on restore). Carried on preview
resolves and on Session.device.

 - PREVIEW_INSTALL_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: No install record on the session row yet (the install has not been
claimed for this boot).
 - PREVIEW_INSTALL_STATUS_PENDING: Install queued; the session VM is still booting.
 - PREVIEW_INSTALL_STATUS_RUNNING: The install-app operation is running on the VM.
 - PREVIEW_INSTALL_STATUS_OK: The app is installed and launched.
 - PREVIEW_INSTALL_STATUS_FAILED: The install failed (artifact download, install, or launch).

v1ResolveClustersResponse.description:
ResolveClustersResponse contains the list of clusters that offer both the
requested image and machine type.

clusters.description: Matching clusters (one entry per cluster that has both image and machine type).

v1ResolvePreviewLinkResponse.description:
ResolvePreviewLinkResponse describes the device session serving this open
plus everything the viewer page needs to attach to it. Re-calling resolve
with the same token is the stream-grant refresh path: it returns the
caller's existing live session (attached=true) with a fresh grant.

appName.description: App metadata from the link, for the viewer page header.

attachOnly.description:
True when the response opens an existing session's device view
(ResolveSessionViewer): the page attaches to that session and never
creates one, so the delete/reopen affordances do not apply and a gone
session is simply gone.

attached.description:
True when the caller was attached to their existing live session for
this link instead of a new one being created.

buildNumber.description: CI build number from the link.

commitSha.description: Built commit SHA from the link.

deviceNotes.description:
Human-readable device detail reported by the VM itself: why the device
FAILED, or how it degraded from the requested configuration while still
working (for example, "requested system image X not installed; using Y").
Empty when the device came up exactly as requested — and always empty for
sessions whose VM scripts predate the signal.

deviceSpec.description: The device spec the link requested.

deviceState.description:
Device readiness verdict, asserted by the VM itself. Visible to anyone
holding the link (resolve is unauthenticated), which is fine: it carries
nothing beyond boot progress.

fallbackReason.description:
Human-readable reason when the link's requested stack/machine type could
not be provisioned and this open fell back to the deployment defaults
(for example, the machine type was retired after the link was minted).
Empty when the session runs exactly what was requested. Only set on the
resolve that created the session — attaches to an existing session
return it empty.

installReason.description:
Human-readable reason why the app install FAILED (the install script's
typed error, e.g. "simctl install failed: … IncompatibleArchitecture …"),
sanitized and bounded server-side. Set only while install_status is
FAILED; empty otherwise, and always empty for sessions written by
backends that predate the field.

installStatus.description: State of the app install on the device.

machineType.description:
Machine type this open's session actually runs on. Empty on sessions
created before this field existed.

sessionId.description: ID of the device session serving this open.

stackId.description:
Stack this open's session actually runs on (the link's requested stack,
the deployment default, or the fallback). Empty on sessions created
before this field existed.

streamBaseUrl.description:
Absolute base URL (scheme + host, no path, no trailing slash) of the
DC-local stream gateway serving this session's media endpoints
(RDE-480). When set, the viewer builds every stream/asset/control URL
against it (base + stream_path etc.) instead of the API host; empty
means the legacy same-host media path. Chosen server-side per session
cluster from deployment config, gated by the enable-rde-stream-gateway
workspace flag and the gateway's live health. The rollout and fallback
levers, with honest latencies for NEW and RECONNECTING connections: a
flag flip lands within one resolve poll (≤3s pre-stream, ≤60s
streaming); the map is deploy config, so changing it takes a pod roll
plus one poll; a gateway OUTAGE additionally waits on health detection
first — the API's probe (15s cadence + up to a 5s timeout), stacked on
the gateway's own cached /readyz self-check (10s cadence + 5s timeout,
demoting a ready gateway only after 3 consecutive failures, ~35s) when
the failure is gateway-side, e.g. a stale token or a severed
gateway-to-control-plane path. Established
streams are never cut by any lever — they migrate on their next
reconnect or at the 30-minute connection cap; the emergency drain of a
live gateway is stopping its process.

streamGrant.description:
Short-lived (max 120s) Ed25519-signed stream grant. The viewer presents
it on the stream WebSocket; it re-calls resolve to refresh before expiry.

streamPath.description:
Path of the stream WebSocket on this API host
(for example, "/ws/preview/{session_id}/stream").

v1ResolveSessionViewerResponse.description:
ResolveSessionViewerResponse carries the viewer bootstrap for a session's
device view — the same message a preview link's resolve returns, with
attach_only set — so the viewer page runs one code path for both.

view.description: The viewer bootstrap: stream grant, gateway routing, device and install state.

v1RestoreSessionResponse.description: RestoreSessionResponse is the response for restoring a session.

v1SavedInput.description:
SavedInput represents a saved credential/value for a user.
Users can reuse these across sessions (for example, GitHub PAT, SSH keys).

isSecret.description: Whether this is a secret value.

value.description:
Value of the input. For secret inputs this is empty unless the request explicitly
set include_secrets=true (see GetSavedInputRequest/ListSavedInputsRequest).

v1ServicePort.description:
ServicePort represents a network service a template's sessions expose on the VM
(for example a dev web server). Sessions snapshot these and the UI renders
SSH tunnel (ssh -L) connection help from them.

description.description: Description shown next to the tunnel help (for example, "Storybook dev server").

localPort.description:
Suggested local port for the tunnel. 0 means "same as port". Use when the
remote port commonly clashes with something on developer machines.

name.description: Short name of the service (for example, "web-app"). Unique per template.

port.description: Port the service listens on inside the VM (1-65535).

v1ServicePortCreate.description: ServicePortCreate is used when creating a service port on a template.

description.description: Description shown next to the tunnel help.

localPort.description: Suggested local port for the tunnel. 0 means "same as port".

name.description: Short name of the service. Unique per template.

port.description: Port the service listens on inside the VM (1-65535).

v1Session.description: Session represents a remote development environment instance.

agentSessionStatus.description:
Current abstract status of the AI agent running in this session.
Provider-agnostic (works for any AI agent). Updated via webhook notifications.

agentSessionStatusUpdatedAt.description: When the agent session status was last updated.

aiConfigured.description:
Whether this session's VM was set up with Claude Code AI tooling.
If ai_enabled is true but ai_configured is false, the session needs a
restart to install Claude Code.

aiEnabled.description: Whether Claude Code AI is available (user has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY configured).

aiPrompt.description: AI prompt passed to Claude Code when the session was created.

autoTerminateAt.description: When the session will auto-terminate. Empty if disabled or already processed by the worker.

autoTerminateMinutes.description: The user's chosen auto-terminate duration in minutes. 0 if disabled.

device.description:
The virtual device this session boots (Android emulator / iOS simulator)
and its live readiness, or absent when the session has no device. This is
the agent contract: a "running" session does NOT mean the device is
usable — poll until device.state is PREVIEW_DEVICE_STATE_READY (and, when
an artifact was supplied, install_status is PREVIEW_INSTALL_STATUS_OK).

labels.description:
Arbitrary key/value metadata attached to the session (for example, team,
branch, ticket id). Returned verbatim; filterable via
ListSessionsRequest.label_selectors.

ownerId.description:
The owner's identifier, typed by owner_type: the owning user's ID for
"user", the workspace slug for "workspace".

ownerType.description:
Who owns the session: "user" (owned by the creating user; the default) or
"workspace" (owned by the workspace itself — for example sessions spawned
by a preview link minted with a Workspace API Token; any workspace member
can see and manage these). Future owner kinds (such as "agent") extend
this value set without a schema change.

persistentDiskStatus.description:
Status of the persistent disk for terminated sessions.
Used to determine if a session can be restored.

sshConnectionOpen.description: Whether the SSH connection is fully established and ready.

templateDeleted.description: Whether the template this session was created from has been deleted.

templateId.description: ID of the template this session was created from (historical reference).

templateOutdated.description:
Whether the template has been updated since this session was created.
Computed by comparing the snapshot's updated_at with the current template's updated_at.
False when the template is deleted or the snapshot predates this feature.

templateSnapshot.description:
Snapshot of the template configuration at session creation time.
Contains all template variables, session input values, feature flags, and workspace links.

updatedAt.description: When the session was last updated.

v1SessionClickResponse.description: SessionClickResponse is the response for clicking.

v1SessionCompleteFileUploadResponse.description: SessionCompleteFileUploadResponse is the response for completing an upload.

v1SessionCompleteUploadResponse.description:
SessionCompleteUploadResponse is the response for completing an upload.

Deprecated: use SessionCompleteFileUploadResponse.

v1SessionDevice.description:
SessionDevice describes a session's virtual device and its readiness — the
same signals the device preview viewer consumes, surfaced on the session
so API/MCP/CLI callers can act on them without a viewer.

appName.description:
App display name from the artifact supplied at creation (the artifact
URL itself is never returned).

buildNumber.description: CI build number from the artifact supplied at creation.

commitSha.description: Built commit SHA from the artifact supplied at creation.

deviceNotes.description:
Human-readable detail from the VM: why the device FAILED, or how it
degraded from the requested configuration while still working. Empty
when the device came up exactly as requested.

installReason.description:
Why the app install FAILED (the install script's own verdict). Set only
while install_status is FAILED. A failed install leaves the device
usable — install the app yourself (simctl install / adb install).

installStatus.description:
State of the optional app install (only meaningful when an artifact was
supplied at creation). UNSPECIFIED = no artifact / not started.

spec.description:
The device this session boots, in the preview link vocabulary: platform
("android"/"ios"), device_model (emulator device profile / simctl device
type), os_version (iOS: the simctl runtime; empty = newest installed),
system_image (Android), and the Android sizing knobs.

state.description:
Device readiness, asserted by the VM itself (see MachineReportDeviceReady):
UNSPECIFIED while the VM is not running, BOOTING once it runs but the
device has not proven itself, READY when the device is booted and its
streamer delivers frames, FAILED when the VM gave up on this boot.

v1SessionDownloadFileResponse.description: SessionDownloadFileResponse is the response for downloading files.

signedUrl.description: GCS signed GET URL for the tar.gz archive.

v1SessionDownloadResponse.description:
SessionDownloadResponse is the response for downloading files.

Deprecated: use SessionDownloadFileResponse.

signedUrl.description: GCS signed GET URL for the tar.gz archive.

v1SessionExecuteResponse.description: SessionExecuteResponse is the response for executing a command.

output.description: Combined stdout/stderr output of the command.

v1SessionInput.description:
SessionInput defines an input that users must or may provide when creating a session.
Configured by the template author. Filled by the session starter.

defaultValue.description:
Default value used in boot scripts when the session starter leaves the field blank.
Only applicable when required is false.

description.description: Description explaining what this input is for.

exposeAsEnvVar.description: Whether to expose this input as an ENV VAR in interactive terminal sessions.

key.description: Key/name of the input (matches saved_inputs.key for auto-prefill).

required.description: Whether this input is required. If false, the input is optional and default_value is used when not provided.

v1SessionInputCreate.description: SessionInputCreate is used when creating a session input definition on a template.

defaultValue.description: Default value when not provided by the session starter. Only used when required is false.

description.description: Description explaining what this input is for.

exposeAsEnvVar.description: Whether to expose as an ENV VAR in interactive terminal sessions.

required.description: Whether this input is required. Defaults to false (optional).

v1SessionInputValue.description:
SessionInputValue provides a value for a session input when creating a session.
Either provide a direct value or reference a saved input by ID (for secrets).

isSecret.description: Whether the value is secret (encrypt at rest). Ignored if saved_input_id is set.

key.description: Key name matching a session input on the template.

savedInputId.description:
Optional: ID of a Saved Input to use. Backend fetches and decrypts the value server-side.
This avoids exposing secret values to the frontend.

value.description: Direct value (used when user typed in a value). Ignored if saved_input_id is set.

v1SessionListScope.description:
SessionListScope selects which sessions ListSessions (and the terminated
cleanup) operates on, by session ownership.

 - SESSION_LIST_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED: Defaults to SESSION_LIST_SCOPE_MINE.
 - SESSION_LIST_SCOPE_MINE: Sessions owned by the calling user.
 - SESSION_LIST_SCOPE_WORKSPACE: Sessions owned by the workspace itself (owner_type "workspace") —
visible to and manageable by every member of the workspace.

v1SessionMouseDragResponse.description: SessionMouseDragResponse is the response for dragging the mouse.

v1SessionNotification.description: SessionNotification represents a persisted notification from a VM.

v1SessionNotificationType.description:
SessionNotificationType defines the type of notification from the VM.

 - SESSION_NOTIFICATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified notification type.
 - SESSION_NOTIFICATION_TYPE_AGENT_STOP: The AI agent has stopped and is waiting for user input.
 - SESSION_NOTIFICATION_TYPE_AGENT_PERMISSION_PROMPT: The AI agent is requesting permission to proceed.
 - SESSION_NOTIFICATION_TYPE_AGENT_IDLE_PROMPT: The AI agent is idle and waiting for a prompt.
 - SESSION_NOTIFICATION_TYPE_AGENT_AUTH_SUCCESS: The AI agent has successfully authenticated.
 - SESSION_NOTIFICATION_TYPE_AGENT_ELICITATION_DIALOG: The AI agent is showing an elicitation dialog.
 - SESSION_NOTIFICATION_TYPE_AGENT_WORKING: The AI agent is actively working (status-only signal, no notification record created).

v1SessionScreenshotResponse.description: SessionScreenshotResponse is the response for taking a screenshot.

signedUrl.description: GCS signed GET URL for the JPEG screenshot image.

v1SessionScrollResponse.description: SessionScrollResponse is the response for scrolling.

v1SessionStartFileUploadResponse.description: SessionStartFileUploadResponse is the response for initiating an upload.

signedUrl.description: GCS signed PUT URL for uploading the tar.gz archive.

uploadId.description: Upload identifier to use when completing the upload.

v1SessionStartUploadResponse.description:
SessionStartUploadResponse is the response for initiating an upload.

Deprecated: use SessionStartFileUploadResponse.

signedUrl.description: GCS signed PUT URL for uploading the tar.gz archive.

uploadId.description: Upload identifier to use when completing the upload.

v1SessionStatus.description:
SessionStatus represents the current state of a session.

 - SESSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified status.
 - SESSION_STATUS_PENDING: Session is being created/provisioned.
 - SESSION_STATUS_STARTING: Session is starting up.
 - SESSION_STATUS_RUNNING: Session is running and accessible.
 - SESSION_STATUS_TERMINATING: Session is terminating.
 - SESSION_STATUS_FAILED: Session creation or operation failed.
 - SESSION_STATUS_TERMINATED: Session is terminated (machine no longer running).
 - SESSION_STATUS_DRAINING: Session VM is being drained off its node (drain in progress, VM still consuming resources).
 - SESSION_STATUS_DRAINED: Session VM was drained and is gone; the session may be restarted to recreate it.

info.description:
API for managing Bitrise Remote Dev Environments (RDE).

> **⚠️ Experimental API.** **Breaking changes may be introduced at any time without notice or a deprecation period.**

## Authentication

All endpoints require a Bitrise Personal Access Token (PAT) sent as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: token <YOUR_PAT>
```

Generate a PAT from your Bitrise account settings.

## Base URL

Production: `https://api.bitrise.io/rde`

## Errors

Non-2xx responses share a single JSON envelope:

```
{
  "code": 5,
  "message": "template not found",
  "details": []
}
```

The `code` field is a numeric status code (not the HTTP status code). Clients should switch on `code` for programmatic handling and surface `message` to humans. Common values:

| HTTP | `code` | Name               | When                                                          |
| ---: | -----: | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
|  400 |      3 | InvalidArgument    | Request validation failed; per-field violations may appear in `details`. |
|  401 |     16 | Unauthenticated    | Missing or invalid `Authorization` header / PAT.              |
|  403 |      7 | PermissionDenied   | The PAT does not have access to the requested workspace or resource. |
|  404 |      5 | NotFound           | The resource does not exist (or is not visible to this PAT). |
|  409 |     10 | Aborted            | Request conflicts with the current resource state (for example, session already running). |
|  412 |      9 | FailedPrecondition | A precondition for the action was not met (for example, session not running yet). |
|  500 |     13 | Internal           | Unexpected server-side failure. Safe to retry with backoff.   |
|  503 |     14 | Unavailable        | A downstream dependency was temporarily unreachable. Safe to retry with backoff. |

post.description:
Turns an app build into a shareable URL that opens the app on a live Android emulator or iOS simulator in the recipient's browser — no Bitrise login, no local tooling, nothing to install. The usual shape is a CI step that builds a simulator/emulator app and posts the link on the pull request, so reviewers can try the change before merging.

## Authentication

Unlike the rest of this API, this endpoint accepts a **Workspace API Token** (`bitwat_…`, created with Remote Dev Environments access) as well as a Personal Access Token — the workspace token is what a CI pipeline should carry, since it belongs to no one person. Devices opened from a PAT-minted link are sessions owned by that user; devices from a workspace-token link are owned by the workspace and are visible to every workspace member. `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/stacks` and `/machine-types` take a workspace token too, so a CI step can check `stack_id` / `machine_type` values before minting.

## Nothing is stored

The signed token in the response is the only artifact — no row is written, and a link nobody opens costs nothing. Every open spawns its own device session, so one link serves many reviewers at once.

## The app build

`artifact.url` must be an absolute http(s) URL that a plain anonymous `GET` can fetch; a presigned URL is fine, and the URL is never echoed back to viewers. It must be a **simulator/emulator** build, not a device build — iOS wants a zipped `.app` carrying an arm64 simulator slice, Android an `.apk` that runs on x86_64. A device-signed build installs on neither.

## Lifetime and limits

`ttl_seconds` defaults to 24 hours and is capped at 72 hours. There is no revocation list, so a short lifetime is the control: treat the link as a bearer credential, because anyone holding the URL can open a device. Sessions a link spawns are capped at 5 alive per link and 20 per workspace — opens past the cap are refused with `ResourceExhausted` — and each one auto-terminates after its idle window (`session_auto_terminate_minutes`, at least 10, default 60).

sessionAutoTerminateMinutes.description:
Idle auto-terminate window (minutes) for sessions this link spawns: a
session ends this long after the last viewer disconnects. 0 uses the
default of 60. When set, it must be at least 10 minutes (a smaller window
would reap sessions mid-boot, before the first viewer stream can extend
the deadline) and at most 480 — the 8-hour session max lifetime always
bounds a session's total runtime regardless of this window, so
auto-terminate can be tuned but never turned off.

deliberately no cluster field — the cluster is derived from the stack +
machine type combination, same as session creation.

Link lifetime in seconds. 0 uses the default of 24 hours; capped at 72
hours. A short lifetime is the primary abuse control — there is no
revocation list, so anyone holding the URL can open a device until the
link expires.

aiPrompt.description: Optional AI prompt to pass to Claude Code when the session starts.

artifact.description:
Optional app build to install on the device once it is ready — the same
message a preview link carries. Requires device_spec. The install runs in
the background; Session.device.install_status reports its progress. The
URL is stored on the session (never returned) so the install can run
without a viewer polling.

autoTerminateMinutes.description:
Minutes before auto-termination. Defaults to 7200 (5 days).
Set to 0 to disable auto-termination ("Never").

cluster.description:
Target cluster name. Required when the template's image + machine type are available
in multiple clusters. If only one cluster matches, this can be omitted.

deviceSpec.description:
Virtual device to boot with this session: an Android emulator (Linux
stacks) or an iOS simulator (macOS stacks) — the same message a device
preview link carries, so links and sessions describe devices identically.
When set:
  - the session boots the device and streams it exactly like a preview
    link's session (see Session.device for readiness);
  - with a template that declares a device (Template.device_spec), the
    request is an override: WITH a platform it is the complete device to
    boot (empty fields = platform defaults, the template's are ignored);
    WITHOUT a platform it tweaks the template's device field by field
    (empty fields inherit); no device_spec at all boots the template's
    device as declared; no_device skips it;
  - stack_id and machine_type may be omitted on a template-less session:
    the deployment's per-platform device defaults apply, and the cluster
    is picked deterministically instead of erroring on ambiguity;
  - a supplied stack/machine type must fit the platform (OS family, spec
    floor) or the request is rejected — no silent fallback.
Absent = no device. auto_terminate_minutes keeps its ordinary default
either way. Gated per platform by the enable-rde-android-emulator /
enable-rde-ios-simulator workspace flags.
